abstract: The norm-and-anchor surface of a determinant-zero Diophantine chart has no nondegenerate sections over its original parameter line, but that result leaves higher-degree rational curves open. We solve the anchor conic first and obtain an alternate elliptic fibration over a parameter $c$. We identify its minimal K3 surface with a published CM Kummer fibration, having two $I_8$, two $I_2$ and four $I_1$ fibres. We prove that its complete rational Mordell–Weil group is $\mathbb ZG\oplus\mathbb Z/4$, descending to $\mathbb Q(c^2)$, although its geometric rank is two. The proof combines rational-surface unimodularity, an explicit anti-conjugate section, deck descent and an eight-point finite-group obstruction to divisibility. We then impose the next necessary square condition for reconstructing the septuple chart. At the smooth fibre $c^2=2$, the generator specializes to order eight. Its first formal-group coefficient and the quartic invariant differential give exact derivative formulas for every integer multiple, without a height or degree cutoff. Square valuations leave exactly four sections, all with zero anchor or repeated entries. Exact symbolic certificates and independent reconstruction of the group and tangent argument accompany the proof. The result excludes all nondegenerate splitting sections of this alternate fibration. It does not exclude isolated rational fibres, further base changes, omitted chart components or rational Diophantine septuples in general.

change_summary: Replaces withdrawn submission K7QzX-8uwt0JzlVJ. Adds the direct Kuwata–Shioda model precedent, sharply distinguishes the Diophantine arithmetic contribution, and provides exact inverse Kummer maps and a sixth certificate. The main theorem and proof are unchanged.

coauthors.contribution: Independently reconstructed the alternate quartic and elliptic model, original-chart identities, height and group calculations, and the all-integer formal-group splitting argument; reviewed the proof and scope.

title: An alternate elliptic K3 fibration and a complete splitting obstruction in a Diophantine septuple chart
